Latest Update: Fascia Release Is the Key to Regulating Your Nervous System, Getting Better Sleep, and Improving Skin

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (867 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Harpersbazaar

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that I’m curled up on a treatment bed in the Corinthia spa, feeling a knot of tension dissipate slowly from my neck and shoulders.
  • Sources indicate that “Fascia is deeply connected to the entire sensory network,” explains Nadia Alibhai, a London-based osteopath who was unfazed by my heightened emotions.
  • Once dismissed as mere biological wrapping paper, fascia—made up of water, collagen, elastin, and hyaluronic acid—is now understood as a living, three-dimensional web.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that I’m curled up on a treatment bed in the Corinthia spa, feeling a knot of tension dissipate slowly from my neck and shoulders. Within minutes, tears prick my eyes. I’m familiar with the sudden catharsis bodywork can bring, but this is different. Known as “myofascial release”—a targeted therapy that works with fascia, the continuous matrix of connective tissue that wraps every muscle, nerve, and organ—it aims to reduce tightness and release restricted tissue, restoring its natural glide.

Sources indicate that “Fascia is deeply connected to the entire sensory network,” explains Nadia Alibhai, a London-based osteopath who was unfazed by my heightened emotions. “When you move or hold stress, forces are transmitted through this interconnected system. It senses everything and dictates how the whole body responds. This treatment directly influences how we perceive and react to tension.”.

Once dismissed as mere biological wrapping paper, fascia—made up of water, collagen, elastin, and hyaluronic acid—is now understood as a living, three-dimensional web. “It’s part of a complex system involving movement, circulation, lymphatics, posture, and tissue health,” Alibhai explains. When it works well, it keeps everything moving and prevents systems from becoming sluggish, but when it becomes restricted, often from scrolling, sedentary habits, or chronic stress, the fluid between the layers can thicken. This affects physical mobility and emotional well-being, leading to complications ranging from pain and stiffness to a dysregulated nervous system.

In a recent development, fascia and neurology are intrinsically linked, explains skin-health expert Annee de Mamiel. “Fascia changes according to how we move, breathe, and repeatedly load the body,” she says. “Cortisol and adrenaline change our physiology; the nervous system alters breathing, muscular tone, and stress response. Over time, these repeated patterns affect the tissues.” It’s a catch-22: greater stress can tighten fascia, which in turn can send your body into fight-or-flight mode, prolonging the anxiety that caused the damage in the first place.

Recent findings suggest that this mind-body connection is just one reason why fascia has piqued the wellness industry’s interest. Google searches for “fascia release” have soared in the past year, while facials targeting the system are becoming more popular. Robert Schleip, the director of the Fascia Research Group at Ulm University, attributes this to its holistic possibilities. “Fascia is now studied in relation to the autonomic nervous system, and therefore emotional regulation, as well as the immune system and aging,” he indicates. The latest findings show that supporting your fascia goes far beyond easing a tight neck; it's linked to reduced arterial stiffness and improved cardiovascular health.

Industry observers note that fascia release has also entered the skin-health conversation. Tight fascia can be an overlooked culprit behind loss of luminosity, puffiness, and premature aging, claims de Mamiel, because it’s heavily involved in fluid drainage and lymphatic pathways. “The diaphragm plays a role in pressure changes and fluid movement through the body, and the fascial system connects these areas,” she explains. “When I work on movement and tension through the neck, chest, and rib cage, I often see a change in how congested or puffy the face appears.” However, releasing fascia effectively doesn't require aggressive force. “If I use so much pressure that your body braces, I’ve produced the opposite response—it’s about creating conditions where the nervous system and tissue can both settle.”.

Facialist Nichola Joss achieves similarly impressive results with her signature Inner Facial, which fuses lymphatic drainage, fascia release, buccal massage, and sculpting techniques. “Fascia surrounds and supports our muscles; when restricted, it affects how freely muscles move,” Joss explains. This affects lymphatic flow and your skin’s natural glow. “By releasing muscular and fascial tension, you lift, tone, and sculpt contours while boosting circulation and softening fine lines.”.

Sources indicate that beyond professional treatments, supporting fascial health depends on consistent daily habits. First, fascia thrives on varied movement: try walking, twisting your body, reaching overhead, and squatting to support overall health. Unfortunately, there are no true quick fixes: Spending the day glued to an office chair and then going straight into an intense HIIT session can actually be counterproductive. Instead, interrupt patterns throughout the day: Stand during phone calls instead of sitting, swing your arms gently during screen breaks, and make sure you’re not holding your breath during stressful periods at work. Counteract hours spent hunched over a device with this simple doorway stretch: Place your forearms against the frame, step forward gently, and hold for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing deeply.

Schleip recommends aligning exercise with your circadian rhythm. “Incorporate dynamic, elastic, or bouncing movements in the morning, ideally outdoors, and slow stretches in the evening,” he suggests, adding that sustained yoga positions, such as a child’s pose held for at least 30 seconds, can be particularly helpful. “Regular stretching improves joint mobility and may benefit cardiovascular markers such as arterial stiffness,” he adds. Finally, make nutrition and hydration a priority: fascia is 70 percent water and needs hydration to glide freely.

As Alibhai reflects at the end of my session: “The goal isn’t to constantly release fascia; it’s to keep your body moving, adaptable, and well nourished.” I leave feeling lighter and more grounded—and I instinctively skip the Tube and walk home.

Our gift guide for men spans everyone on your list, from the teen boy who’s into fitness and skincare to the hardworking dad who never treats himself to the polished guy who seems to already own everything worth owning.

According to recent reports, while a gift card technically counts as a present, we think our picks are more memorable. Keep scrolling for unique, practical, and elevated ways to treat him, no matter the occasion.

Recent findings suggest that if your guy lives for athleisure, he’ll appreciate Forme’s smart joggers. The brand states that the high waistband offers extra support across his lower back and core, helping to stabilize his posture without being too restricting. In other words, these joggers are working just as hard as he is.

The latest Oura ring comes with some pretty cool updates. Most noticeably, it’s 40% thinner than previous models and its battery can last up to nine days on a single charge. It still tracks health metrics like sleep, temperature, activity, and heart rate, but the upgraded sensors can now give him more precise readings.

This cashmere sweater will be a staple in his wardrobe (and he’ll think you spent so much more on it than you did!).

Home chefs and grill masters will love this powerful pepper cannon that shoppers stated saves them so much time.

In a recent development, half the fun of having a boyfriend, male bestie, or brother is dressing them up like a Ken doll. Consider this you sign to upgrade their tired polo collection with this much cooler street style version.

He’ll feel so spoiled with these luxe cufflinks that you can customize with his initials or another meaningful engraving.

Breathable, silky, and supportive, these boxer briefs could very well become his new favorites. Underwear with holes and worn-out elastic, out you go!

If he’s particular about his pour, he’ll get a kick out of this. He just loads in a can or bottle of his favorite beer and pulls the handle for a draft-style glass with a thick, creamy head of foam. It runs on batteries, so he can bring it to tailgates.

It has been revealed that his pockets can only hold so much. This compact nylon bag fits his phone, keys, and wallet, with a zippered exterior pocket for valuables and an adjustable strap he can wear around his waist or across his chest.

If America’s pastime is his favorite sport, get him a hard-bound history of his home team. There are 31 teams to choose from, even the storied Brooklyn Dodgers.

Industry observers note that make sure he has at least one high-quality hoodie hanging in his closet. Lululemon’s Steady State SuperLoft pullover is roomy, sturdy, and made of extra-soft fleece. Choose from 11 colors.

Industry observers note that fidget toys, but make them cool and executive. Seriously: the silver design and the sleek gift box make this the perfect gift for your favorite corporate office-dweller.

Your man deserves to be comfy cozy too, and he’ll love these snuggly woven Uggs for your date nights in.

If he's not jazzing up his suits with funky dress socks, he's missing out. This navy pair hits the perfect sophisticated-to-fun ratio.

Industry observers note that the golfer in your life will love these links-ready shoes from Travis Mathew’s St. Andrew’s collection. They feature the signature tartan, superior traction and support, and pressure point tested replaceable spikes.

Frosting is for the guys, too. This David Yurman bracelet is a timeless piece that adds polish to any look. The minimal design works just as well with a T-shirt as it does with something dressier. 10/10, Andie Anderson would approve.

Beef up his daily prep routine with this set from Marlowe. It doesn’t have any added fragrances that could irritate sensitive skin, and the shea butter and aloe formulas will give him a deep cleanse without drying out his skin.

If he’s going to spend his Sunday yelling at the television, he might as well look good while doing it...

This one’s for the guy who loves to lounge with his e-reader, tablet, or phone. Clip a small receiver onto the device, and use the remote to click through the pages. Fun bonus: He can set up the clip to take photos with his phone using the remote.

13 Pairs of Gloves to Keep Your Digits Toasty All Winter Long

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that there are few winter experiences more miserable than stepping outside with bare hands and realizing, too late, that your fingers have stopped working.
  • Some turn a quick phone check into a whole production; others are so bulky you might as well be wearing oven mitts.
  • According to recent reports, these luxurious leather gloves come from Overland, the brand behind some of our favorite coats.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that there are few winter experiences more miserable than stepping outside with bare hands and realizing, too late, that your fingers have stopped working. First they’re freezing, then they’re numb, and before long your skin feels dry and rough and beyond the help of any hand lotion.

But honestly? Gloves can be annoying, too. Some turn a quick phone check into a whole production; others are so bulky you might as well be wearing oven mitts. The best winter gloves keep your hands warm without making your fingers useless—and look good while they’re at it. We’ve rounded up our favorites, from waterproof, windproof pairs built for rough weather to stylish options that still keep your hands nice and toasty. And yes, plenty have touchscreen-compatible fingertips so you can still call and text (and play the Wordle). See our favorite pairs below.

According to recent reports, these luxurious leather gloves come from Overland, the brand behind some of our favorite coats. The smooth leather looks very polished, so these gloves can be dressed up if you want, but they go just as well with a casual outfit. They’re also quite durable and are naturally water-repellant, and the cashmere lining adds warmth on the inside.

In a recent development, commerce Editor Luke Guillory loves these merino wool-lined deerskin gloves from Geier Gloves, a brand that has been making leather products in the U.S. for almost a century. Since the brand specializes in leather, you can bet the deerskin on these gloves is of the highest quality, and the wool lining is very nice, too. Geier also makes a lot of wor, driving, and motorcycle gloves, so you know they’re the real deal. The black and brown colorways look quite polished, but the natural and saddle leather options are also great.

If you want a nice luxurious pair of cashmere gloves, go with these ones from Sunspel. Lately, I’ve been wearing these gloves, which were knitted in Scotland from super soft pure cashmere. The brand has been perfecting the craft for over 150 years, so you can trust that these are the best of the best. It’s basically like enveloping your hands in a cozy blanket. For a full set, get the brand’s cashmere hat and scarf.

Sources indicate that these Canada Goose gloves are basically the equivalent of wearing a puffer jacket on your hands. With heavy-duty, long rib-knit cuffs for extra protection and 750-fill-power down on the inside, your hands will stay warm and dry without their mobility being super impacted by something extra bulky. Note that these have a touchscreen-compatible index finger but not thumb.

Recent findings suggest that wool-blend gloves are as handsome as any of the very best sweaters in your rotation. Even though the outside is made from knit material, the insulated interior will keep your hands warm and dry during your next epic snowball fight. They’re also thin enough to layer under another pair of gloves if it’s really freezing outside.

When it comes to gloves, there’s one brand I’ve trusted for years, and that’s Smartwool. Their gloves are warm without being bulky, and mine have lasted for years. Having a warm pair of gloves that actually does its job well is even more important for my boyfriend, who has Raynaud’s and needs extra protection for his hands, and the gloves he relies on year after year? Also Smartwool. These new fleece gloves from the brand have extra insulation on the back to provide serious warmth, and they’re also functional with touchscreen-compatible pads on the thumbs and index fingers. Sure, they’re a little expensive for fleece gloves at $68—but if you don’t need the extra insulation, you can try the regular Active Fleece Gloves for $48.

If all you need is a solid pair of knit gloves and you’re not looking to spend a fortune, look no further than Uniqlo. The brand’s Heattech knit gloves are soft and warm and have effective touchscreen-compatible fingertips. They also come in 11 fun colors, so you might as well get a couple pairs for yourself—and they make a great holiday gift for literally anyone.

You already know we love Barbour’s waxed canvas jackets, so it’s no surprise we’re also a fan of the brand’s stylish, preppy gloves. These leather-palmed gloves have a cotton tartan face for a cool contrast and wool lining on the inside for extra warmth—and they’re waterproof, so you can break them out no matter what’s going on with the weather. Pair these with the Barbour Beaufort jacket for an iconic look.

It has been revealed that knit gloves are great when it comes to keeping warm, but they’re not the best when it’s raining or snowing. No one wants a pair of soaking gloves (that probably make your hands feel even colder). Enter these waterproof gloves from the brand that brought you the famous Bean Boots. With a waterproof nylon exterior and a down fill, they’ll keep rain and show out while keeping your hands warm. Note that some say the fingers are long, so consider that when choosing a size.

In a recent development, when you’re stuck in a blizzard or your location is prone to unpredictable weather, you’ll need something a little more heavy duty. REI’s weatherproof gore-tex gloves will give your hands the protection they need. They’re also essentially a two-in-one: The removable fleece liners can be used on their own or with the weatherproof outers as an extra layer of warmth.

Naadam’s famous cashmere sweater is one of our favorite pieces of winter clothing and one of our go-to gifts for the holidays, birthdays, Valentine’s Day, etc. The brand makes a matching pair of soft cashmere gloves, which come in 13 colors and are under $100. A genius gift idea? Get them the sweater with a matching pair of gloves, and they’ll wear both all winter long.

If you want that classic Sherlock Holmes leather glove look, you have lots of choices. But if you don’t want to spend a ton on a pair, get these $60 gloves from Quince. Not only do they have a nice leather exterior in either brown or black, they also have a cashmere lining on the inside.

On the high end of the high end, Gucci has a gorgeous luxury pair of leather gloves with the brand’s signature horsebit on the wrist for a fun little detail. Made from leather and silk, these are soft, smooth, and very stylish.
